heroLead: West Waynesburg sits right beside Waynesburg, the Greene County seat, in what's widely considered some of the richest wet gas ground in the entire Marcellus play.
intro: If there's one county in Pennsylvania where we tell people to slow down before signing anything or selling anything, it's Greene County. This is core Marcellus ground, some of the thickest, most liquids-rich shale in the play, and West Waynesburg sits right in the middle of it. That also means it's ground where getting the details right matters more than almost anywhere else in the state.
We take that seriously with every West Waynesburg interest we review, because a mistake here costs more than it would somewhere with thinner production.

sections.heading: Why Greene County Ground Is Different
paragraphs: Greene County sits at the heart of the Marcellus wet gas fairway, with some of the thickest shale and richest liquids content anywhere in the play, and operators including EQT, CNX, and Southwestern have all developed extensive acreage here over the years. That intensity of development means West Waynesburg-area units often have longer production histories and more data behind them than newer or less active counties.

It also means competition for interests here can be real, which is exactly why we make sure any offer we give reflects your unit's actual performance, not a lowball number banking on you not checking.

sections.heading: The Utica Adds Another Layer
paragraphs: Beneath the Marcellus in Greene County sits the deeper Utica-Point Pleasant formation, which some operators have begun developing as a separate target on the same acreage. If your lease covers all formations rather than the Marcellus alone, that could mean additional value sitting below your existing production that hasn't been captured yet.
We check what formations your lease actually covers, because a Marcellus-only lease and an all-depths lease can be worth very different amounts on ground like this.

sections.heading: Deductions Hit Harder When Volume Is Higher
paragraphs: Ironically, being in such productive ground means post-production deductions can eat a larger absolute dollar amount out of your check, even at the same percentage rate, simply because there's more volume to apply them against. We've seen West Waynesburg owners genuinely surprised by how much a gathering or compression line item actually costs them once the math is laid out clearly.

faqs.question: Is West Waynesburg really in the best part of the Marcellus?
faqs.answer: Greene County is widely regarded as core wet gas ground with some of the richest shale in the play, though your specific unit's production history still determines actual value.

faqs.question: Does my lease cover the Utica formation too, or just the Marcellus?
faqs.answer: It depends on how your lease defines the leased formations. We review this specifically because Utica rights can add meaningful value beyond current Marcellus production.

faqs.question: Why do deductions seem larger here than what I've heard from other areas?
faqs.answer: Higher production volume means the same deduction percentage translates into a larger dollar amount. We break this down clearly when reviewing your statement.
